title: Osie Johnson, Claude Hopkins and other D.C. names
summary: Phillips says Osie Johnson was 17 when he played with them in 1943, did not know Claude Hopkins's relatives, and mentions pianist Dick Hopkins.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Who else did you run into around here? How about Osie Johnson?
That was later. His name was James, but everybody called him "Osie."
Phillips - 180
Was he from D.C.?
Yeah, he was born here. See, he wasn't but 17 years old when he was playing with us -- John.
In that picture in 1942-43?
Yeah, '43. He was just 17 years old.
How about Claude Hopkins? Of course, Claude Hopkins was already gone by the time you got here.
Oh yeah.
He has some relatives around here. Did you ever know any of them?
No. None of them.
I've seen some of his relatives around here.
I didn't.
A real short fellow, one of his cousins or something.
What did he do?
I don't know. I just saw him in a club one night.
Was he playing?
No. He was just walking around, this guy.
There's a guy named Dick Hopkins, but he's not related to... He's a piano player. Dick is a little short, fat guy. He plays a whole lot of piano. He works down at Market End.
But not related to Claude.
No.
